nodes.label: Gradient
nodes.description: Linear, radial or angular grayscale ramp.

nodes.label: Checkerboard
nodes.description: Checkerboard of Color 1 and Color 2, Columns squares across and Rows down.

nodes.label: Grid
nodes.description: White grid lines on black, Columns cells across and Rows down, Thickness as a share of a cell’s shorter side so lines are as thick across as down. X Offset slides each row along by that much of a cell more than the one before it, and Y Offset each column down: 0.5 staggers alternate rows like brickwork, and a smaller one steps them into a diagonal.

nodes.label: Bricks
nodes.description: Running-bond brick pattern with mortar, bevel and per-brick tone variation.

nodes.label: Shape
nodes.description: A primitive shape as a mask, ready to use in one node. Every shape 2D SDF Shape draws, and Dome, a rounded height rather than a flat one: Circle, Ellipse, Square, Rhombus, Diamond, Parallelogram (Skew), Trapezoid (Top Width), Triangle, Isosceles Triangle, N-gon of Sides sides, Star of Points points with its hollows at Inner Radius, Hexagram, Cross, X, Heart, Egg (Point), Teardrop, Vesica (Narrowness), Crescent (Bite), Cut Disk (Kept), Pie and Arc (Sweep degrees), Tunnel, Stairs (Steps), Capsule (Top Size), Gear of Teeth teeth cut Tooth Depth into its rim, Cloverleaf, Line, Arrow, Chevron and Spiral of Turns turns. Thickness is how wide the drawn ones are. Each faces up where it has a way to face. Size is the shape across; Stretch X and Y make a circle an ellipse and a square a rectangle; Corner Rounding rounds the corners of shapes that have them; Outline keeps only a band Outline Width wide inside the edge, for rings and frames. Softness fades the edge inward, Rotation turns the shape clockwise and Centre places it. For many copies, feed it into Scatter. A shape placed across an edge comes back in at the other, so it tiles. To join shapes smoothly, cut one from another, offset, ring or repeat them, start from 2D SDF Shape instead.

nodes.label: 2D Fractal Noise
nodes.description: Octaves of the Basis noise, each Lacunarity times the frequency and Diminish times the strength of the last, 0 to 1 about the middle at any number of octaves. Ridged octaves give sharp crests, Billow round lobes. Clouds, dirt, grime and every organic variation start here; one octave is plain Perlin or Value noise. Octaves finer than the image can show fade out, so a preview and a bake look alike.

nodes.label: 2D Worley Noise
nodes.description: Cellular noise: a jittered point in every cell, and for each pixel the nearest of them, by the Metric — Euclidean round cells, Manhattan diamonds, Chebyshev squares. Channels hold the nearest one to four: their distance, or what Style picks instead — the cell value, the cracks between cells, the next one out, or dots at the points. Octaves layer finer cells over coarser ones, for stone and crystal. Cell Value at Jitter 0 is a grid of flat random squares.

nodes.label: 2D White Noise
nodes.description: An independent random value in every cell, with no relation to its neighbours: grain, sensor noise, per-tile variation. Uniform spreads the values evenly; Gaussian gathers them about the middle, as film and sensor grain do. At the largest Scale every pixel has its own, at any resolution.

nodes.label: 2D Blue Noise
nodes.description: True blue noise, ranked by void and cluster: whatever threshold is taken, the cells above it are spread as evenly as they can be, without clumps or gaps. For dithering, stippling and even scattering. Scale is cells per repeat, up to one a pixel; above 64 it is a multiple of 64, tiles of the pattern laid side by side.

nodes.label: 2D Anisotropic Noise
nodes.description: Fractal noise drawn out into streaks, Anisotropy times longer than they are wide, running Horizontal or Vertical: brushed metal, fibres, wood grain, streaked rust. Tiles; turn it afterwards for another direction.

nodes.label: 2D Gabor Noise
nodes.description: Sparse Gabor noise: short wave packets scattered over the image, each Frequency cycles to a cell, turned Angle give or take Spread. Local and oriented rather than a pattern of whole-image waves — scratches of grain, fabric weave, sanded and brushed surfaces. Spread 180 is every direction. Impulses is how many packets each cell holds; Bandwidth how short they are.

nodes.label: 2D Wave Noise
nodes.description: Waves across the whole image: Waves sine waves spread by Spread degrees around Angle, at Scale cycles per repeat. Their interference makes wood grain, ripples and moiré; for waves in short local packets, use 2D Gabor Noise.

nodes.label: 2D Flake Noise
nodes.description: Metallic flakes, as in car paint: discs of random size, Coverage of the cells holding one, Scale of them across the image — the larger, the smaller the flakes. Output is 1 on every flake less up to Variation, which Variation Seed draws per flake — so the values can be reshuffled without moving a flake — and 0 between them. Normal is a tangent-space normal map of the flakes, each facing its own way up to 45° from straight out and flat between them; blend it into a surface's normal with Normal Blend, which can also weaken it. Presence is how near the surface each flake sits, for deciding where they overlap.

nodes.label: 2D Curl Noise
nodes.description: Curl of a fractal potential: a swirling, divergence-free flow field, X in red and Y in green, encoded like a normal map. Unlike two channels of Fractal Noise, the flow never gathers or spreads, so what it warps folds into swirls rather than pinching. Amplitude 1 fills the image at any number of octaves. Feed it to a warp for smoke, liquid and marble.

nodes.label: Constant
nodes.description: A constant value: a color from the picker, a float or vector whose components are unbounded, a 2 × 2, 3 × 3 or 4 × 4 matrix on a matrix wire, a boolean (stored as 0 or 1), or one of a list of named choices, which carries the index chosen. Int keeps a float, vector or matrix to whole numbers, and makes a float an integer.

nodes.label: Ramp Left-Right
nodes.description: Linear ramp from Left (U = 0) to Right (U = 1).

nodes.label: Ramp Top-Bottom
nodes.description: Linear ramp from Top (V = 1) to Bottom (V = 0).

nodes.label: Ramp 4 Corners
nodes.description: Bilinear ramp between the four corner values.

nodes.label: Split Left-Right
nodes.description: Left of U = Center is Left, right of it is Right, with an antialiased edge.

nodes.label: Split Top-Bottom
nodes.description: Below V = Center is Bottom, above it is Top, with an antialiased edge.

nodes.label: Random Float
nodes.description: A stable random value between Min and Max for each distinct In value, such as a cell or flake ID.

nodes.label: Random Color
nodes.description: A stable random RGB color for each distinct In value, with hue, saturation and brightness drawn from their ranges.

nodes.label: Blend
nodes.description: Composites the foreground over the background using a blending mode: Normal, which lays the foreground on, or one of Burn, Darken, Difference, Dodge, Divide, Exclusion, Hard Light, Hard Mix, Lighten, Linear Burn, Linear Dodge (Add), Linear Light, Linear Light Add Sub, Multiply, Negation, Overlay, Pin Light, Screen, Soft Light, Subtract and Vivid Light. The result is kept between 0 and 1. Mask decides how much of the blend lands where — black leaves the background showing, white lets the blend through — and Opacity does the same for the whole image at once. The two multiply, so a mask at half under an opacity of a half is a quarter.

nodes.label: Blur
nodes.description: Softens the input over Radius, in image widths, so a preview and a bake blur alike. Box averages evenly out to Radius; Gaussian falls off smoothly, reaching nearly nothing at Radius; Kawase is a fast, soft stand-in for a large gaussian. Bilateral keeps edges sharp, blurring only across values closer than Edge Threshold. Anisotropic stretches a gaussian along Angle (clockwise from pointing right), narrowing it across by Anisotropy — at 1 a straight streak. Slope smears up the slope of the Slope input, Radius far. Flow smears along the directions of the Flow input, curving with them, Radius each way — brushed metal, hair, wood grain: Angle reads it as grayscale, 0 to 1 for a full turn clockwise from pointing right; Vector as red right and green down, 0.5 meaning still, as Spline Direction Field draws, where a shorter vector smears less. Radial zooms towards Centre or spins about it, by Amount of the distance or of half a turn. Median takes the middle value, removing specks and keeping edges. Map Driven blurs each pixel by Radius × Amount.

nodes.label: Warp
nodes.description: Moves the input’s content, with Map saying how far, in image widths times Intensity. Directional pushes everything towards Angle (clockwise from pointing right); Gradient pushes it down the map’s slopes, away from its bright parts, as if they were raised and the image slid off them — Radius is how broad a slope it feels, and Intensity 1 moves a pixel on a slope rising 1 over a tenth of the image by a tenth of the image; Vector pushes along the Vector input, red right and green down with 0.5 standing still, as Spline Direction Field draws it, so an image streams along a path; Radial pushes out from Centre, further the further out a pixel already is, fading to nothing half a tile away so the result still tiles; Churn smears several ways at once, evenly around the circle from Angle, and brings everything it passed back together — averaged, which churns a surface instead of smearing it one way, or the darkest or lightest of it, which eats into shapes or grows them along the map, for chipped and worn edges. Steps walks a strong warp in that many small steps, each turning with the field, so it flows round shapes instead of folding over itself. Path decides what a stepped warp gives back: End is where the walk finishes, the warp itself; Average blends everything it passed, streaking the image along the flow; Darkest and Lightest keep the darkest or lightest of it, which with Gradient wears edges away down the map’s slopes or builds them up — chipped paint, eroded stone, dripping grime. The more Steps, the smoother the streak.

nodes.label: UV Transform
nodes.description: Scales, turns and moves the input. Scale X and Scale Y are its size — 2 is twice as big, 0.5 half — along the image’s own axes, so a square texture stretches into a brick or a plank; a turned stretch stays a stretch rather than becoming a shear. Rotation turns it clockwise and Offset moves it, in image widths. A copy smaller than the image repeats as Sampling says; to repeat a whole image a number of times, Tile It is the node for it. Connect UV to transform coordinates of your own rather than the texture’s. Pixel Exact constrains the transform to one that rearranges texels without blending any — a quarter turn, a whole scale ratio and a whole number of texels — so a mask stays as crisp as it was.

nodes.label: Height to Normal
nodes.description: Converts a height map to a tangent-space normal map encoded in [0, 1], with +Y up the image (OpenGL). Depth is how tall a height of 1 stands, as a share of the texture’s width — the same Depth Height to AO, Height to Shadow and Height to Bent Normal take, so a normal, its occlusion and its shadows made from one height agree on how deep it is. Filter takes the slope from the texels either side (Central) or weighs the rows around them in too (Sobel), which is smoother on a sharp or noisy height. A DirectX map, with Y the other way, is written by choosing that convention when exporting.

nodes.label: Height to Curvature
nodes.description: Curvature from a height map, measured at Radius (in UV, so resolution-independent). Combined is 0.5 on flat areas, brighter on ridges and edges, darker in cavities; Convex and Concave isolate one side for edge wear or dirt masks.

nodes.label: Fresnel
nodes.description: Fresnel reflectance from a tangent-space normal map, viewed straight on: low where the surface faces you, rising to 1 where it turns away. Power sharpens the falloff; IOR sets how reflective it is face-on (glass, 1.52, gives 0.04).

nodes.label: Height to AO
nodes.description: Ambient occlusion from a height map: how much surrounding relief within Radius hides each point from the sky. Depth is how tall a height of 1 stands, as a share of the texture’s width — the Depth Height to Normal and Height to Shadow take, so a normal map, its occlusion and its shadows agree on how deep the relief is. Intensity strengthens or weakens the result. The search looks in many directions at once, sixteen sets of them blended, so the result is smooth, free of grain, and the same at any resolution. Sampling says what lies past the edge: Repeat tiles, a border treats the image as a decal with nothing around it.

nodes.label: Normal to Height
nodes.description: Recovers the height a tangent-space normal map implies, by solving for the surface whose slope it is. Depth is how tall a height of 1 stands — set it to the Depth the normal map was made at and Height to Normal’s height comes back as it was — and 0.5 is the level that was flat. Nothing is cut off: a relief taller than 0 to 1 comes back taller. A normal map records which way the surface faces and never how far it rose, so for one whose depth no one knows, Fit to Range stretches the height to run from 0 at its lowest to 1 at its highest. Tileable. A flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Normal to Curvature
nodes.description: Curvature from a tangent-space normal map, measured at Radius (in UV, so resolution-independent). Combined is 0.5 on flat areas, brighter on ridges and edges, darker in cavities; Convex and Concave isolate one side for edge wear or dirt masks. A normal map carries no scale, so Intensity sets the strength.

nodes.label: Normal to AO
nodes.description: Ambient occlusion from a tangent-space normal map: the height it implies is solved for, then each point is asked how much of the surrounding relief within Radius hides it from the sky. The relief is as deep as the normal map says — the occlusion Height to AO gives the height it was made from — and Intensity strengthens or weakens the result. Tileable. A normal map records no absolute height, so a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Bevel
nodes.description: Bevels the edge of a shape: how far each pixel lies from the edge, up to Width in image widths, as a height. Inner rises inside the shape, Outer outside it, and Both makes one ramp through the edge, which is what a normal map wants. Profile shapes the rise: Linear is a straight chamfer, Smooth eases both ends, Rounded is a bullnose — steep at the edge, flat on top — and Cove the hollow reverse. The distance is exact to a fraction of a pixel at any Width, so narrow gaps — mortar between bricks, cracks between tiles — bevel as cleanly as wide ones. Threshold says where the edge of a soft shape is. Sampling decides whether a shape at one edge of the image bevels against the opposite one, as a tiling texture needs. Distance, under Masks, is the same measure made for masks.

nodes.label: Morphology
nodes.description: Grows or shrinks what is bright in an image, by Radius in image widths. Dilate takes the largest value within reach, so bright shapes swell and dark gaps close; Erode the smallest, so bright shapes thin and dark gaps open. Open erodes then dilates, which removes bright specks and threads narrower than Radius and leaves everything larger as it was; Close dilates then erodes, which fills dark pits and cracks the same way. Each channel is taken on its own, so it works on heights, masks and colors alike — a height dilated stays flat-topped, as a worn stamp would. Round reaches the same distance every way; Square reaches further on the diagonals, but costs half as much. Sampling decides whether a shape at one edge reaches across to the opposite one.

nodes.label: Glow & Shadow
nodes.description: A glow or a shadow around a shape, for decals, labels, stickers and raised lettering. Outer Glow spreads out from the shape and Inner Glow in from its edge; Drop Shadow falls Distance away towards Angle (clockwise from pointing right) beneath it, and Inner Shadow falls inside it, as if it were cut into the surface. Radius is how far the effect reaches, in image widths; Spread makes the first part of that solid before it fades, for a harder edge. Out is the effect as a layer — Color, with the effect as its alpha — ready to blend under or over the shape; Mask is the effect alone. Each is kept off the shape (outer effects) or within it (inner ones), so the shape can be laid over or under it without a fringe.

nodes.label: Sharpen
nodes.description: Sharpens by adding back, Amount times over, the detail a blur of Radius would remove. Radius is in image widths, so a preview and a bake sharpen alike: a small one crisps fine texture, a large one lifts the local contrast of whole shapes — the broad, punchy kind of sharpening — without touching the overall levels. Threshold leaves flat areas alone, so fine noise is not amplified with the detail.

nodes.label: High Pass
nodes.description: Keeps what an image has finer than Radius and takes away the rest: the image less its blur, around a middle grey. A gradient of light across a photograph, a vignette, any shading broader than Radius falls away; texture, grain and edges stay, ready to become height or detail, or to be laid over a flat colour with an Overlay blend. Radius is in image widths, so the same detail is kept at any resolution; Strength scales what is left.

nodes.label: Emboss
nodes.description: Reads the input as a height and lights it from Angle (clockwise from pointing right): slopes facing the light brighten, slopes facing away darken, over mid grey. Depth is how tall a height of 1 stands, as a share of the image’s width — the Depth Height to Normal takes, so the two agree — and a slope tilted 45° towards the light reads white. Distance is how far apart, in image widths, the slope is measured, so a larger one softens fine detail; both are the same at any resolution. Grayscale, since an embossed color is neither the color nor the relief.

nodes.label: Edge Detect
nodes.description: Finds edges in the input, as a mask. Sobel is the usual choice; Prewitt weights every neighbour alike; Laplacian finds thin lines rather than slopes. Width spaces the samples, in image widths — never closer than a pixel — so a wider setting finds softer edges and a preview finds the edges a bake will. What comes out is how much the brightness changes across Width: a hard edge from black to white is 1, times Amount; Threshold takes off the weakest, and Invert turns the mask over.

nodes.label: Swirl
nodes.description: Twists the input about Centre. The turn is Angle at the centre — clockwise for a positive angle, as every rotation in the app turns — and nothing at Radius, so the swirl blends into what surrounds it; Falloff shapes how quickly it lets go.

nodes.label: Tile It
nodes.description: Repeats the input in a grid of X by Y cells, with the whole input in each one. X Offset shifts every row along by that fraction of a cell and Y Offset shifts every column, so half an offset gives the staggered arrangement of brickwork. Each copy can be varied so the repeat stops showing: Mirror flips every other column and row; Random Flip mirrors that share of the copies, Random Rotation turns that share by a random quarter, Random Scale shrinks copies by up to that much about their middles — leaving the cell around them empty, like grout — and Random Offset slides each copy’s content by up to that share of a cell. Seed deals another set. The variation repeats with the grid, so the result still tiles. Sampling decides what happens at the cell edges: Repeat keeps a tileable input seamless across them, a border shows its color between them.

nodes.label: Make Seamless
nodes.description: Makes an input tile, so its left edge meets its right and its top meets its bottom. Blend cross-fades the image with itself shifted half a tile, which keeps the middle of the image untouched and spends Blend Width near the edges hiding the join; it keeps the detail but softens a band around the seam. Seam Noise breaks those bands into an organic edge, so they stop reading as a straight cross; Seed picks another edge. Mirror folds the image instead, which is exact and keeps every pixel sharp, but halves what is on show and makes it symmetrical. This node always wraps, since that is what being seamless means.

nodes.label: Soft Threshold
nodes.description: Cuts a mask out of a gradient: everything below Position goes to black and everything above to white, with Contrast deciding how abruptly. Slide Position to choose how much of a noise survives, and raise Contrast to harden the edge — at 1 it is a clean threshold, at 0 a ramp across the whole range. The usual first step in turning a noise into a shape.

nodes.label: Value Squeeze
nodes.description: Squeezes the whole range into a band of width Range centred on Position. Nothing is thresholded away, only made shallower — which is how a height map is kept from using up all of its depth, or a mask kept from ever reaching pure black. At Range 1 and Position 0.5 it does nothing.

nodes.label: Value Band
nodes.description: Keeps a band and discards the rest: values near Position come out white and those far from it black. Range sets how wide the band is and Contrast how soft its sides — at 1 the band has hard edges, at 0 it falls away from the middle to nothing at the edge. Picks one layer out of a gradient, where Scan would take everything above a level.

nodes.label: Value Cycle
nodes.description: Moves every value along by Shift and wraps it round, so what runs off white comes back from black. Nothing is squeezed and nothing is lost — the range is rotated rather than remapped — which makes it the one of these that can be undone exactly.

nodes.label: Auto Range
nodes.description: Stretches the image so its darkest value lands on Low and its brightest on High, whatever they happened to be. A noise that only ever runs from 0.2 to 0.7 uses the whole range afterwards, without anyone having to find those numbers by hand — which is what makes this the one to reach for after a blur, a blend or a warp has quietly narrowed a map. Unlike the other histogram nodes it looks at the whole image, so it costs a pyramid to work out. All channels are stretched by the one mapping, taken from brightness, so a color keeps its hues rather than being pulled apart.

nodes.label: Equalize
nodes.description: Spreads the image’s values evenly from 0 to 1: the darkest goes to 0, the brightest to 1, and every stretch between holds as much of the image as any other. Where Auto Range only stretches the ends apart, this also evens out the middle, so a map bunched around a few values uses the whole range — a height that is mostly flat with a few peaks, or a noise pulled thin by a blend. Luminance equalizes brightness and keeps hues; Per Channel spreads each channel fully but shifts colors. Amount mixes back towards the input. The histogram is taken in 256 levels from up to 128 × 128 samples of the image: values packed closer together than one level stay together.

nodes.label: Scatter
nodes.description: Places Pattern many times over the image, each copy with its own size, angle and shade. Mode decides where they go: Grid lays X Amount by Y Amount of them, every other row moved along by Stagger (half gives brickwork), each Scale of its cell across; Random places Count copies Size across anywhere, spread evenly enough that none is far from the next but in no grid — pebbles, rivets, debris; Radial puts Count copies in a ring Radius from the middle, and Face Outward turns each to point away from it. Rotation turns every copy clockwise. Random Scale shrinks each copy by up to that share of its size, Random Rotation turns it up to that many degrees either way, Random Offset moves it up to that share of the way to its neighbour, and Random Value darkens it — each from its own part of the seed, so turning one up leaves the others as they were. Density thins the copies out, and a Mask thins them where it is dark, read once per copy so a copy is wholly there or wholly gone. Blend decides what overlapping copies do: Max joins them, which is what a height or a mask wants; Add accumulates; Over lets later copies cover earlier ones by their alpha. Tileable: a copy running off one edge is the same copy arriving at the other.

nodes.label: Scatter Atlas
nodes.description: Scatter where each copy may be a different shape, taken from an atlas. Everything works as it does in Scatter; what is added is Atlas Columns, Atlas Rows and Atlas Count, which say how the atlas is laid out so a copy can pick a cell of it at random. Set them to match the Create Atlas that made it — a texture carries pixels, not the arrangement they were put in, so this cannot be read from the image. A cell left empty in the atlas scatters as a copy that does not appear.

nodes.label: Create Atlas
nodes.description: Lays several shapes out in a grid as one image, for Scatter Atlas to pick from — the difference between a field of identical pebbles and a field of pebbles. Slots fill the grid in reading order; Columns and Rows set its shape, and Count how many of the slots are used. A cell with no slot behind it is left empty rather than repeating the last one, which is how you ask for a copy that sometimes does not appear. Give Scatter Atlas the same Columns, Rows and Count.

nodes.label: Distance
nodes.description: Measures how far every pixel is from the nearest edge of a mask, out to Distance in image widths. Grow pushes the mask outwards, fading from 1 inside it to 0 at Distance away; Shrink eats it inwards from its own edge; Signed gives both at once with the edge sitting at a half, which lets a Levels afterwards slide the outline in or out without solving anything again. Profile shapes the fade — Linear, Smooth, Rounded or Cove — as Bevel’s does; Bevel is the same measure made for heights. The edge is placed to a fraction of a pixel where an antialiased mask crosses Threshold, so the fade is as smooth as the mask. Nearest gives every pixel the Source color at the nearest pixel inside the mask — or the mask’s own, with nothing wired — which spreads colors outward into the gaps: mortar filled with the brick beside it, a texture’s edges padded with what lies just inside them. Sampling decides whether a shape against one edge is close to the opposite edge too, so a tiling mask stays tiling.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Shape
nodes.description: A primitive shape as a signed distance field: every pixel holds how far it is from the edge, in image widths, negative inside. Thirty-one shapes, from Circle, Ellipse, Box and polygons to Star, Hexagram, Heart, Egg, Vesica, Cut Disk, Tunnel, Stairs, Capsule, Gear and drawn ones such as Line, Arc, Cross, X, Arrow, Chevron and Spiral. Size is the shape across; Aspect sets how tall a box, ellipse, rhombus, isosceles triangle or tunnel is against its width; Corner Rounding rounds every corner without changing the size. Combine shapes with 2D SDF Combine, reshape them with 2D SDF Modify, Transform and Repeat, and turn the result into an image with 2D SDF to Mask. The field wraps at the image edge, so it tiles. For a plain mask in one node, use Shape under Patterns: the same shapes, with Softness, Outline and Stretch of its own.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Combine
nodes.description: Combines two signed distance fields. Union keeps everything either holds, Subtract cuts B out of A, Intersect keeps only where both are, XOR keeps where one is but not both, and Morph blends A into B by Amount. Join shapes the corner where the shapes meet: Sharp leaves it crisp, Smooth fills it with a rounded fillet and Chamfer with a straight bevel, Smoothness wide — the way two shapes melt into one. An unconnected input holds no shape.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Union
nodes.description: Joins up to six signed distance fields into one, each to those before it: everything any of them holds. Join shapes where they meet — Sharp leaves a crisp corner, Smooth a rounded fillet and Chamfer a straight bevel, Smoothness wide — so a cluster of shapes melts into one form in one node rather than a chain of Combines. ID tells the parts apart: each pixel takes a value for the input nearest it, a sixth for A up to 1 for F. An unconnected input holds no shape.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Blend
nodes.description: Melts two signed distance fields together the way metaballs do, each carrying a color or an image of its own — wire a texture into Color A and a different one into Color B, and where the shapes run into each other the textures do too. Falloff is how the shapes pull together: Exponential is soft; Classic metaball reaches further, drawing shapes together from further apart with fuller necks between them; Polynomial is tight, touching nothing more than half of Smoothness away. Smoothness is how far shapes reach to join; Color Blend is how wide the change from one color to the next is, from a hard line at 0 to a long soft fade. Color is the blended image, filling the whole frame, with the joined shape as its alpha; 2D SDF is the joined field, to go on through Modify, To Mask or another blend; Mask is the shape alone. Weight is B’s share of every pixel, from 0 where it is all A to 1 where it is all B: wire it into a Blend’s mask to mix a roughness, a height or a whole material along the same melt. For more than two shapes, chain blends, or melt many copies with 2D SDF Scatter. An unconnected field holds no shape and gives no color.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Modify
nodes.description: Reshapes a signed distance field. Offset moves the edge out by Amount, or in when negative — growing a shape rounds its corners, shrinking it sharpens them. Onion hollows the shape into a band Thickness wide around its edge, and Rings repeats that, splitting each band in two, for rings within rings. Invert swaps inside and outside. Displace pushes the edge in and out by the Map — a noise gives rough, worn or wavy outlines — Amount at most either way, where 0.5 in the map leaves it.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Transform
nodes.description: Moves and reshapes a signed distance field about the image's middle, keeping it a distance field. Offset moves it, Rotation turns it clockwise and Scale X and Y size it. Mirror X and Y fold it across the middle, so one half is reflected onto the other — the quick way to a symmetrical shape. Elongate X and Y pull the two halves of the shape apart and fill the gap with its middle, turning a circle into a capsule and keeping its ends round. Bend curves the shape, more the further along it a point is. The field is read from its input’s pixels, so scaling up enlarges them and rounds corners by a pixel or two of the input: make a shape the size it is wanted in 2D SDF Shape, and scale down rather than up, for the crispest edges.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Scatter
nodes.description: Scatters copies of a signed distance field, each copy the whole input made smaller, placed as Scatter places its copies — the same Seed gives the same copies in both. Grid lays X Amount by Y Amount of them, every other row moved along by Stagger (half gives brickwork), each Scale of its cell across, so at 1 neighbours touch; Random places Count copies Size across anywhere, spread evenly enough that none is far from the next but in no grid — pebbles, rivets, spots, debris; Radial puts Count copies in a ring Radius from the middle, and Face Outward turns each to point away from it — petals, spokes, a clock face. Rotation turns every copy clockwise; Random Scale shrinks each by up to that share of its size, Random Rotation turns it up to that many degrees either way and Random Offset moves it up to that share of the way to its neighbour. Density thins the copies out, and a Mask thins them where it is dark. Every copy is measured where it reaches, its neighbours’ included, so the field runs on unbroken from one copy to the next and can be offset, glowed or smoothly joined across them. Join decides how copies meet: Separate keeps each its own shape; Melt runs them into one another like metaballs, Smoothness wide, as 2D SDF Blend does, with the same Falloff choices: Exponential, soft; Classic metaball, reaching furthest with the fullest necks; Polynomial, tight. Color gives each copy a color of its own and blends them as the shapes do, over Color Blend when melting: Color From takes the Color image under each copy’s centre — a gradient or a noise gives every blob its own tint — or lays the image onto each copy, a random cell of it per copy when Atlas Columns, Rows and Count say it is an atlas. Its alpha is the shape. ID gives every copy a value of its own, for a shade or a height per tile. Repeat before combining, so the copies can be joined, cut and rounded together.

nodes.label: 2D SDF to Mask
nodes.description: Draws a signed distance field as a grayscale image. Fill is the shape, white inside. Stroke is a line Width wide along its edge. Bevel is a height rising from the edge to white at Width inside, shaped by Profile: Linear is a chamfer, Round a quarter round, Smooth an S-curve flat at both ends, Concave a cove. Outer Glow fades from the edge to nothing at Width outside, and Inner Glow does the same inward. Contours draws lines every Spacing, Width thick, like the height lines of a map. Distance shows the field itself: grey at the edge, white Width inside and black Width outside. Offset moves the edge out, or in when negative, before any of them; Softness blurs the edges, which are never harder than a pixel, so they stay smooth at any resolution. Invert swaps black and white. Normal is the image as a height made into a normal map, as Height to Normal would at the same Depth — but worked out from the field itself, so a bevel’s normals are as smooth as its curve at any resolution, with no stepping.

nodes.label: Mask to 2D SDF
nodes.description: Turns any mask into a signed distance field — how far every pixel is from the mask's edge, in image widths, negative inside — so a painted, generated or imported shape can be combined, grown, hollowed and repeated like a 2D SDF Shape. The edge is placed where an antialiased mask crosses Threshold, between pixels, so the distances are true to a fraction of a pixel and a bevel made from them is smooth. Threshold decides what counts as inside. Sampling decides whether a shape against one edge is measured from the opposite one too, as a tiling texture needs.

nodes.label: Spline to 2D SDF
nodes.description: Turns curves into a signed distance field — its own curve, or every curve on its Spline input — measured to the curve itself, so it is exact at any resolution where a field made from a mask is only as good as the mask’s pixels. Fill is the inside of every curve, each taken as closed, by Rule as Spline Fill decides it. Stroke is a band Width wide along every curve, following each point’s thickness, with round ends. Distances are measured out to Range, and further than that reads as Range: keep it as far as anything downstream reads — an offset, a glow, a bevel — and the field is quick however many curves there are. Tile lets a curve crossing an edge reach the other side.

nodes.label: Polar Transform
nodes.description: Bends a flat image round into a disc, or flattens a disc back out. Wrap reads the input’s x as an angle and its y as a radius, so a horizontal ramp becomes a sweep round the middle and a row of bricks becomes a cobbled ring; Unwrap does the reverse, laying a disc out as a rectangle with angle running across it. The two are exact inverses, so you can unwrap, work on the result as an ordinary tiling image, and wrap it back. Repeat sends the image round more than once, and Rotation turns the whole thing clockwise.

nodes.label: Height Mix
nodes.description: Blends two maps by which of them is higher, rather than by mixing them — so a layer settles into the low parts of what is under it instead of averaging with it. Wire the heights to Height A and Height B to decide the contest with maps other than the ones being blended; leave them and each map is its own height. Opacity tips the contest toward B rather than fading between them, and Transition is how sharply the two meet — zero cuts along the contour where they are level, wider feathers it. Mask decides where the layer applies at all, fading back to A where it is black — which is a different control from Opacity, that tips the contest rather than hiding its result. The Mask output carries the decision the node made, so the base color, roughness and normal of a layered material can all be blended by the same one.

nodes.label: Spline Path
nodes.description: A curve you draw, as a spline for other nodes to use. Select it to edit the curve in the 2D View: drag a point to move it, click the curve to add one, and alt-click one to take it away. Interpolation decides how the curve passes its points: Smooth runs through every one; Bézier does too, steered by two handles on each point that the 2D View shows — dragging one turns the other with it, and holding Alt breaks the pair for a corner; Quadratic is pulled towards each point without passing through it; Linear joins them with straight lines. Closed joins the last point back to the first. Wire the Spline output into Spline Render to draw it, or into any other spline node.

nodes.label: Spline Paths
nodes.description: Several curves drawn in one node, as a spline with a curve for each path — for cracks, veins or stalks drawn many at a time. Select it to edit the paths in the 2D View: click a path to work on it, then drag, add and remove its points as on Spline Path. New Path in Properties starts another, Delete Path removes the one being worked on, and Closed joins its ends. Interpolation applies to every path.

nodes.label: Spline Circle
nodes.description: A circle as a spline, as round as the largest bake can show. Polygon turns it into a regular polygon of Sides sides — three is a triangle, six a hexagon — and Arc takes less than the full turn, which leaves an open curve rather than a loop. Start Angle turns the shape; Centre and Radius place and size it, as fractions of the image.

nodes.label: Spline Shape
nodes.description: A shape as a spline. Rectangle and Rounded Rectangle are Size X by Size Y, the rounded one with Corner Radius on its corners — panels, plates, frames. Star has Points points reaching Radius, its notches Inner Radius of the way in. Spiral winds Turns times from Inner Radius of the way out to Radius — coils, springs, a snail’s shell. Line runs Size X across. Centre places the shape and Rotation turns it, clockwise. Spline Circle makes circles and regular polygons.

nodes.label: Spline Render
nodes.description: Draws curves as strokes: its own curve, or every curve on its Spline input when one is wired. Select it to edit its own curve in the 2D View. Width sets the stroke, scaled at each point by that point’s own thickness, so a line can taper; Cap rounds or squares off the ends. The Height output gives the stroke a profile — Round like a cable, Linear like a ridge, Flat like a plateau — times each point’s height, ready for Height to Normal. Weave makes strands alternate over and under wherever they cross, as in a basket or a fabric, and Weave Depth is how far a strand dips to pass under. ID gives every curve a value of its own (per Seed), Along runs from 0 to 1 along each curve, and Distance is a field 0.5 on the stroke’s edge, reaching 1 and 0 at Distance Range inside and out. Tile brings a curve that runs off one edge back in at the other.

nodes.label: Spline Fill
nodes.description: Fills the inside of curves as a mask: its own curve, or every curve on its Spline input. An open curve is filled as though a straight line joined its ends. Rule decides what counts as inside where curves overlap: Non-zero fills everywhere they wind round, Even-odd fills every other layer, so a curve inside another cuts a hole in it. Tile lets a shape crossing an edge fill on both sides of it. ID gives every shape a value of its own, per Seed — the same a Spline Render of its curve gives it — so traced stones or tiles can each take their own colour or height; an island inside a hole is a shape of its own. Bevel rises from 0 at the edge to 1 at Bevel Width inside, ready to become a height.

nodes.label: Spline Ribbon
nodes.description: Lays an image along curves as a ribbon: its x runs along the curve and its y across it, so a strip of bricks follows a path and a rope winds round a loop. Width is the ribbon, scaled at each point by its thickness. Stretch fits one copy of the image to the whole curve; Repeat lays copies Tile Length × Width long, so a square image stays square however long the curve. Corners: Mitre turns the image round a corner as a picture frame’s moulding does, squeezed inside and stretched outside; Round has each pixel take the nearest point of the curve, which fans the image round the outside of a corner. Connect a Start or End image for pieces of their own at the ends of an open curve, Piece Length × Width long — frayed ends on a rope, posts at the ends of a fence — and the middle repeats a whole number of times between them so it meets both cleanly. Slide moves the middle along the curve, Flip turns the image over across it. The UV output is where each pixel read its image, for UV Transform to lay something else the same way; Mask is the ribbon itself.

nodes.label: Spline Direction Field
nodes.description: Draws a flow map along curves: a direction in red and green, with 0.5 meaning still — feed it to Warp in Vector mode to stream an image along a path. Along points the way each curve is heading; Outward points away from the curve on either side, to push things off it. Intensity is the strength on the curve, fading to nothing at Width/2 away; Falloff shapes the fade, from 0 (full strength to the edge) up. Reverse turns every direction round.

nodes.label: Spline Transform
nodes.description: Moves, turns and scales every curve on its Spline input about a pivot. Scale X and Scale Y stretch along the image’s own axes before the turn, so a stretched curve stays stretched when turned; Rotation turns clockwise. Scale Thickness carries the scale over to the stroke, so a curve shrunk to half is drawn half as thick.

nodes.label: Spline Reverse
nodes.description: Runs every curve on its Spline input the other way. Everything a curve’s direction decides turns round with it: which side Spline Offset moves it to, where Along starts, which way Spline Direction Field points and text along it reads, and which way a closed curve winds, which Spline Fill’s Non-zero rule counts. A closed curve keeps its first point, so it still starts where it did.

nodes.label: Spline Smooth
nodes.description: Rounds off the corners and steps of every curve on its Spline input: each vertex moves towards the average of the curve within Radius of it, so a traced outline loses its staircase and a jagged line flows. Strength mixes between the curve as it was and fully smoothed. Corners turning more sharply than Corner Angle stay sharp and the smoothing stops at them, so a square keeps its corners while its sides relax; at 180 nothing is kept. An open curve’s ends stay put, and a closed one shrinks a little, as anything averaged does. A curve with few points has little to move — Spline Resample it first for an even, fine one.

nodes.label: Spline Randomize
nodes.description: Varies every curve on its Spline input on its own, each by amounts of its own from Seed. Random Thickness and Random Height lower a whole curve’s thickness and height by up to that much of themselves — cracks of differing depth, planks of differing wear, strands of differing weight. Random Scale and Random Rotation scale and turn each curve about its middle by up to that much either way, and Random Offset moves it up to that far, so copies from Spline Array or Spline Instancer stop looking like copies.

nodes.label: Spline Warp
nodes.description: Moves every point of the curves on its Spline input by a map read where the point is. Intensity pushes each point out along the curve’s normal by the map’s brightness — black leaves it where it is, and Two Sided makes mid-grey the still point so dark pulls one way and light the other. Vector moves it by the map’s red and green, 0.5 being still, as Warp and Spline Direction Field read them. Amount is how far, as a fraction of the image.

nodes.label: Spline Sample
nodes.description: Sets what each point of the curves carries from a map read where the point is. Height is what Spline Render’s Height output stands the curve up by; Thickness is what scales its stroke there. Copy replaces the value with the map’s, Add and Subtract change it by the map’s, Multiply scales it by the map’s. Amount scales the map first. A thickness never goes below zero.

nodes.label: Spline Profile
nodes.description: Sets the thickness and height of every curve on its Spline input along its length, from two gradients whose left end is each curve’s start and right end its finish: white is full, black is nothing. Use it to taper, bulge or pinch a stroke, or to make a ridge rise along its length, however many points the curve has. Multiply scales what each point already carries; Replace sets it outright.

nodes.label: Spline Trace
nodes.description: Traces the outlines of a mask into curves: every edge where the mask crosses Threshold becomes a closed curve, holes included, running the opposite way round so Spline Fill leaves them empty. Find Islands cells become stone outlines to bevel with Spline Render; a painted crack becomes a curve to warp or wiggle. Detail is how finely the mask is read — finer follows smaller shapes and costs more — and Smallest leaves out outlines of fewer steps than that, the specks of a noisy mask. With Tile on, an outline that runs off one edge continues from the other. At most 1024 outlines.

nodes.label: Spline Text Outline
nodes.description: Sets text as the Text node does and gives back the outline of every letter as a curve, the counters of a, e and o included, for engraved, outlined or bevelled lettering: stroke it with Spline Render, fill it with Spline Fill, or offset it into a rim with Spline Offset. The letters are set by the browser and traced, so Detail is how closely the outline follows them — 256 keeps the corners of a large word crisp. Each letter outline is one curve; at most 1024 in all.

nodes.label: Spline Trim
nodes.description: Cuts every curve on its Spline input down to the stretch between Start and End, as fractions of its length. Offset slides that stretch along the curve, and round and round a closed one. Raise End from 0 to 1 and a stroke draws itself along its curve, which is how a mask grows along a path. A cut curve is open; a stretch of no length draws nothing.

nodes.label: Spline Dash
nodes.description: Cuts every curve on its Spline input into dashes Dash long with Gap between, each dash a curve of its own — stitching along a seam, a dashed line, a row of perforations. Offset slides the pattern along the curve by that much of a dash and its gap, which animates a march or lines two rows up. Round a closed curve the dashes are stretched slightly to go round a whole number of times, so the seam hides; an open curve’s ends cut whatever dash they meet. Draw them with Spline Render, or scatter a stitch along each with Spline Scatter. At most 1024 dashes in all.

nodes.label: Spline Resample
nodes.description: Lays the vertices of every curve on its Spline input out again, evenly along its length: Count of them on every curve, or one every Spacing, so a long curve gets more. More than a curve had keeps its shape and makes it finer for Spline Warp or Spline Wiggle to bend; fewer cuts its corners, for a low-poly look. A closed curve stays closed.

nodes.label: Spline Wiggle
nodes.description: Gives every curve on its Spline input a hand-drawn wobble: each is laid out again finely and pushed to either side by a smooth noise of how far along it is. Amount is how far, Wavelength how long one wave is along the curve, and Octaves adds finer wobble on top. Because it is measured along the curve, the wobble keeps its pace on a long curve and a short one alike, and round a closed curve it comes back to where it started. Each curve wobbles its own way; change Seed for another.

nodes.label: Spline Offset
nodes.description: Moves every curve on its Spline input out to its side by Offset, keeping the same distance all along it — corners stay sharp. A closed curve grows for a positive Offset and shrinks for a negative one, whichever way it was drawn; an open one moves below a curve drawn left to right. Copies makes more, each Spacing further out, for parallel lines, rings or contour lines from one curve.

nodes.label: Spline Simplify
nodes.description: Holds every curve on its Spline input with fewer vertices, dropping each one the curve can do without while staying within Tolerance of where it was. A smooth curve of many small steps comes down to a few; raise Tolerance and it becomes a hand-cut, low-poly line. The first and last vertices always stay, and a closed curve stays closed.

nodes.label: Spline Hang
nodes.description: Hangs a cable between the points of a curve: every span from one point to the next sags into the curve a chain makes under its own weight, by Slack times its length, so a long span sags further than a short one. Angle turns which way is down, clockwise; a negative Slack bows the spans up. Draw the pegs on its own curve, or give it curves on its Spline input, whose every vertex is a peg — a Linear path, or Spline Resample to space them out. Thickness and height run evenly from peg to peg.

nodes.label: Spline Growth
nodes.description: Grows branching curves from seeds, for cracks, roots, veins, coral and lightning. Trunks start from places scattered over the image, or all from one Point, heading Direction (clockwise from pointing right) give or take Spread. Each walks Segments steps along its Length, turning by up to Jitter at every step. Every curve sprouts Branches children, down to Depth generations; a child leaves from along its parent’s middle at Branch Angle, alternating sides, and is Branch Length times as long. Taper thins each curve towards its tip, and a child starts as thick as its parent was there, so the tree thins towards its ends — the thickness also becomes each point’s height, so a crack is deepest at its trunk. At most 1024 curves.

nodes.label: Spline Flow Lines
nodes.description: Draws curves that follow a map, for wood grain, water streaks, hair and currents. Count lines start on a grid over the image, each nudged by Jitter, and walk Steps steps of Step Length the way the map points where they are. Vector reads the map’s red and green, 0.5 being still, as Warp’s Vector mode and Spline Direction Field make it — a still place stops a line; Angle reads its brightness as a heading, 0 pointing right and 0.25 down. Feed it a blurred noise for grain, or a Spline Direction Field for lines that run alongside other curves. Taper thins both ends to nothing. At most 1024 lines.

nodes.label: Spline Append
nodes.description: Puts the curves of up to four inputs into one list: those on A, then B, then C, then D, each unchanged. Use it to draw, fill or scatter along several curves with one node — a fill of two curves under Even-odd makes a ring.

nodes.label: Spline Join
nodes.description: Joins every curve on its Spline input into one, in order: each runs on from the end of the one before, crossing the gap in a straight line. Closed joins the end of the last back to the start of the first. A curve can hold only so many points, so a very long join is thinned evenly along its length.

nodes.label: Spline Pick
nodes.description: Keeps some of the curves on its Spline input, by their place in the list, which starts at 0. Range keeps Count of them from Start; Every keeps every Step-th from Start; Random keeps each with a chance of Probability, a different set for each Seed. Invert keeps the rest instead.

nodes.label: Spline Loft
nodes.description: Runs Count strands between curves, each from the same place along every curve it joins. Between runs them from the last curve on A to the last curve on B, like the rungs between two rails; Through runs them through every curve on A in turn, first to last. Smooth curves the strands — between two curves each leaves square to them, through a list it passes smoothly through every curve — and Detail is how finely each curved stretch is walked. The strands are a spline like any other, and Spline Loft Ribbon lays an image across them.

nodes.label: Spline Loft Ribbon
nodes.description: Stretches an image across the strands on its Spline input — wire in Spline Loft — so it fills the space between the curves the loft was built on and bends with them. The image’s x runs from the first strand to the last, its y along each strand; Flip turns it over along the strands. The UV output is where each pixel read the image, for UV Transform to lay something else the same way; Mask is the area the strands cover.

nodes.label: Spline Instancer
nodes.description: Places copies of the curves on Shape along the curves on Path, as Spline Scatter places images. Draw the shape around the middle of the image — that is the point placed on the path. With several shape curves each copy takes one at random. Mode decides where they go: Even spaces Count copies along each path curve by distance; Random puts Count copies anywhere along it. Size is how wide the whole image the shape was drawn in becomes at each copy. Follow Curve turns each to the way the path heads, Rotation turns them all clockwise, Offset slides them off it to one side, and Scale Thickness scales each copy’s stroke with it. Random Scale shrinks each copy by up to that share of its size, Random Rotation turns it up to that many degrees either way, and Random Offset moves it up to that share of the way to its neighbour along the path. Density thins the copies out, and a Mask thins them where it is dark. The copies are a spline, so they can be drawn, filled, warped or scattered along in turn.

nodes.label: Spline Array
nodes.description: Copies every curve on its Spline input. Linear lays Count copies in a row, each Step X and Step Y further on — panel lines, rungs, a run of planks. Grid lays Columns × Rows of them, Step X across and Step Y down — tiles, rivets, a tread. Radial turns Count copies about Centre, spread evenly round a full turn of Angle or from first to last over less — vents, petals, the spokes of a wheel — clockwise for a positive Angle. Every copy is a curve of its own, so Spline Randomize can vary them. At most 1024 curves in all.

nodes.label: Spline Text
nodes.description: Sets a string along a curve — its own, or every curve on its Spline input — each character turned to the curve where it sits. Select it to drag its own curve in the 2D View. Along slides the string from one end to the other, Across lifts it off the curve so it can sit above or below the line, and Flip reads the curve backwards for text that would otherwise be upside down. The glyphs are drawn at the resolution the pass renders at, so they stay crisp at any size.

nodes.label: Spline Scatter
nodes.description: Places copies of a shape along a curve — its own, or every curve on its Spline input. Select it to drag its own curve in the 2D View. Mode decides where they go: Even spaces Count copies along each curve by distance, so they stay even through a bend, and Closed spreads them the whole way round a loop without doubling up at the join; Random puts Count copies anywhere along it. Up to 16384 over every curve together. Size is a copy’s width in image widths. Follow Curve turns each copy to the direction the curve is heading there, Rotation turns them all clockwise, and Offset slides them off the curve to one side or the other. Random Scale shrinks each copy by up to that share of its size, Random Rotation turns it up to that many degrees either way, Random Offset moves it up to that share of the way to its neighbour along the curve, and Random Value darkens it. Density thins the copies out, and a Mask thins them where it is dark. Blend decides what overlapping copies do, as on Scatter. Copies that run off an edge arrive at the other, so the result tiles.

nodes.label: Spline Scatter Atlas
nodes.description: Places copies along curves — its own, or every curve on its Spline input — where each copy may be a different shape, taken from an atlas. Everything works as it does in Spline Scatter; what is added is Atlas Columns, Atlas Rows and Atlas Count, which say how the atlas is laid out so a copy can pick a cell of it at random. Set them to match the Create Atlas that made it — a texture carries pixels, not the arrangement they were put in, so this cannot be read from the image. A cell left empty in the atlas scatters as a copy that does not appear.

nodes.label: Kuwahara
nodes.description: Smooths an image without crossing its edges, which leaves it looking painted. Radius is the brush, in image widths, so a preview and a bake paint alike. Every other blur asks what the neighbourhood averages to; this asks which part of it is most uniform and answers with that part’s average — so a flat area flattens further while an edge survives, because the part lying along one side of it is far more uniform than any part straddling it. Classic uses four overlapping quadrants, which is the original and the cheapest, and shows as blockiness on anything curved. Generalized cuts a disc into Sectors and weighs each by how uniform it is rather than letting one win outright, which is smooth where Classic steps; Sharpness decides how strongly uniformity is preferred. Anisotropic first asks the image which way it is changing and squashes the disc into an ellipse lying along each edge, so the sectors follow a curve the way a brush does; Anisotropy sets how far an ellipse may stretch — at 0 it is Generalized, and even turned up a flat area stays round, having no direction to stretch along. It costs a few passes more than the others. Alpha passes through. Tileable.

nodes.label: Crop
nodes.description: Takes a rectangle of the input, given by its Left, Right, Top and Bottom edges. Stretch fills the output with it, so cropping is also zooming in; Keep leaves the rectangle its own size and in its own place and clears everything else, which makes the node a rectangular mask instead. Rotation turns the rectangle about its own centre, so a crop can follow something that is not square to the image. Dragging an edge past its opposite narrows the rectangle rather than turning it inside out.

nodes.label: Auto Crop
nodes.description: Finds the rectangle the content actually occupies and crops to it, without anyone having to measure it. Threshold decides what counts as content, and Measure chooses whether that is how bright a pixel is or how opaque — an image placed on nothing carries its shape in alpha rather than in its color. Padding leaves a margin, so a shape does not end up touching the edge of its own image. Stretch fills the output with the rectangle; Keep leaves it where it is and clears the rest. An image with nothing above the threshold has no rectangle to crop to and is handed back as it came.

nodes.label: Height to Shadow
nodes.description: The shadow a height map casts on itself from a single light. A ray is walked towards the light from every point, climbing at the light’s Elevation, and anything standing above it shuts the light out. Angle turns the light around the surface and Elevation raises it: low light throws long shadows, overhead light almost none. Depth is how tall a height of 1 stands, as a share of the texture’s width — the Depth Height to Normal and Height to AO take, so they agree — Distance how far a shadow may reach, and Softness how quickly its edge gives way. Unlike ambient occlusion this has a direction to it — a pit is dark in both, but only here does the dark sit to one side. Sampling says what lies past the edge: Repeat tiles, a border treats the image as a decal with nothing around it.

nodes.label: Height to Bent Normal
nodes.description: The direction each point is most open to the sky in, from a height map. A normal map says which way a surface faces; in a groove that may be straight up while everything above it is wall, and what light arrives comes from along the groove instead. Lighting a cavity with this is what stops it reading as a flat surface with a dark patch painted on. Radius sets how far the search looks, and Depth how tall a height of 1 stands — the Depth Height to Normal and Height to AO take. Sixteen sets of directions are blended, so the result is smooth at any resolution. Sampling says what lies past the edge.

nodes.label: Normal UV Transform
nodes.description: Scales, rotates and offsets the coordinates a normal map is read at, turning the stored vectors by the same angle so the relief stays lit from the direction it now faces. Use this rather than UV Transform whenever what is being moved is a normal map. Scale X and Scale Y are the map’s size along the image’s own axes, 2 twice as big, as they are there: a plain transform moves the picture and leaves the vectors pointing the old way. Connect UV to transform coordinates of your own rather than the texture’s. Pixel Exact constrains the transform the way it does on UV Transform — a quarter turn, a whole scale ratio and a whole number of texels — which matters more here: the vectors are then turned by that same quarter, so every normal that comes out is one that went in.

nodes.label: Normal Blend
nodes.description: Combines two normal maps, putting Detail on top of Base. Adding them channel by channel is wrong in a way that looks almost right — the sum of two unit vectors is not one — so pick a mode instead. Reoriented turns the detail into the base’s frame, so a bump on a slope leans with the slope; it is the most correct and the one to reach for. Whiteout is cheaper and keeps detail crisp, flattening a steep base a little. Slopes adds the two surfaces’ slopes, which is what combining their heights would have done. Replace keeps only the detail. Strength leans the detail before it is combined, so turning it down leaves the base as it was rather than fading everything towards flat.

nodes.label: Normal Normalize
nodes.description: Puts every vector in a normal map back to one unit long. Anything that treats a normal map as a picture — a blur, a resize, a lossy file — leaves vectors that are no longer unit length, and a shader lighting those gets the strength of the relief wrong rather than obviously broken. Rebuild Z throws the stored blue away and works it out from red and green, which is what makes a two-channel normal map whole again. Strength leans the vectors further from or closer to straight up, which is the part that carries the relief.

nodes.label: Normal Rotate
nodes.description: Turns every vector of a normal map about straight up by Angle, without moving a pixel — so the relief is lit as though it ran another way. Connect a map to Angle to turn each pixel its own way, Angle times the map: a flow or angle map lays brushed metal, wood grain or weave along a curve. Normal UV Transform turns the vectors the same way at the same Rotation, but moves the pixels with them; use this when the picture is to stay where it is.

nodes.label: Skew
nodes.description: Leans the image over: Horizontal slides each row sideways by how far down it is, Vertical slides each column up or down by how far across it is. The slide is measured from Centre, so that line stays put and the image leans about it rather than drifting off. Amount is in whole UV, so 1 slides the far edge a whole repeat — which for a tileable image is no slide at all, and is why whole amounts keep it tiling.

nodes.label: Mirror
nodes.description: Folds the image about a line, replacing everything past it with its reflection. Position sets where the fold is, and Flip chooses which side is kept. Both folds along each axis in turn, giving four of the same quarter. Folding makes the two edges of an axis meet whatever was there before, so this is also the blunt way to make an image tile — at the cost of showing half of it twice, and of a crease down the fold. Kaleidoscope folds round Centre instead: one wedge of the image, reflected and repeated Segments times round, for rosettes, medallions, rims and wheels; Rotation turns which wedge is kept, clockwise.

nodes.label: Normal to Bent Normal
nodes.description: The direction each point is most open to the sky in, from a tangent-space normal map: the height it implies is solved for, then each point is asked which way the relief within Radius still leaves open. The relief is as deep as the normal map says. Tileable. A normal map records no absolute height, so a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Find Islands
nodes.description: Finds the separate shapes in a mask — runs of lit pixels that touch — and gives each one an identity of its own. Blue is a value per shape, the same everywhere within it and unrelated to its neighbours, which is what drives a color, a roughness or a height per shape. Red and green hold the shape’s identity, equal for two pixels exactly when they are in the same shape. Alpha is 1 inside a shape. Wire Shape into any of the island readers — one wire is all each takes. Threshold sets what counts as lit, Diagonals decides whether shapes meeting only at a corner are one shape or two, Sampling decides whether a shape touching one edge continues on the other, and Quality is there for the rare mask whose shapes wind so far that the settling needs longer — if a shape comes back as two values, raise it.

nodes.label: Island Random Value
nodes.description: Gives every shape found by Find Islands a grey of its own, the same everywhere in that shape and unrelated to its neighbours’. The usual way to vary a height, a roughness or a mask per shape rather than per pixel. Seed deals a different set of values without changing which shapes there are.

nodes.label: Island Random Color
nodes.description: Gives every shape found by Find Islands a color of its own. Mostly for seeing the shapes — a field of them in flat colors shows at a glance which are separate and which have been joined. Saturation pulls the colors towards grey, for tinting rather than confetti.

nodes.label: Island Order
nodes.description: Where each shape falls in reading order — down the rows first, then along them — as a value from 0 at the top-left-most shape towards 1 at the bottom-right-most. Measured against the image rather than against the number of shapes, so it is an order and not a count: adding a shape does not renumber the others, and the values are not evenly spaced.

nodes.label: Island UV
nodes.description: Where each pixel sits inside its own shape’s box: red runs 0 to 1 across the shape and green down it. The coordinates to read something per shape with — feed them to a UV Transform, or use them to place a gradient or a pattern inside every shape at once.

nodes.label: Island Size
nodes.description: How big each shape’s box is, as a fraction of the image: red is its width, green its height and blue the larger of the two. Fills each shape with its own size, so a mask can pick out the large shapes from the small ones.

nodes.label: Island Ramp
nodes.description: A ramp across every shape at once, running 0 to 1 over each shape’s own box towards Angle (clockwise from pointing right). Random Angle turns each shape’s ramp by its own amount, so a field of them does not read as one ramp cut into pieces.

nodes.label: Island Random Pick
nodes.description: Picks a random share of the shapes found by Find Islands: white for the ones kept, black for the rest, each shape whole. Probability is the share kept — the missing bricks of a wall, the cracked tiles of a floor, the few rusted plates of a hull. Seed picks a different set without changing how many; the same Seed and a higher Probability keeps every shape it kept before, and more.

nodes.label: Island Stamp
nodes.description: Puts a copy of Image into every shape found by Find Islands, fitted to that shape’s own box — so one authored detail fills a field of shapes of different sizes. Fit stretches each copy to its box, or keeps the image square, as large as fits. Scale grows or shrinks each copy from the middle of its shape and Rotation turns them all (clockwise). Then each copy is varied by its own shape: Random Rotation turns it by up to that share of a full turn — in quarter turns with Quarter Turns on, which keeps a pixel image crisp — Random Scale shrinks it by up to that share, and Random Offset moves it by up to that share of its box. So a field does not read as the same picture stamped over and over. Anything outside a copy is left empty rather than smeared, and the image’s alpha comes through.

nodes.label: Island Sample Color
nodes.description: Fills every shape found by Find Islands with the single color or value that Image holds at the middle of that shape. One reading per shape rather than per pixel, so each shape comes out flat and the pattern across them is the image’s — which is how a field of shapes takes its colors from a gradient, a photograph or a noise. A shape whose middle lies outside it — a ring, an L, a crescent — is read at a point of its own instead, so it never takes a neighbour’s color.

nodes.label: Facing Mask
nodes.description: A mask from which way a surface faces, read off its normal map. Direction picks out the slopes turned towards Angle (clockwise from pointing right, so 270 is up the image) and Elevation, how far that direction rises out of the image: snow and dust on the tops of stones, moss on one side, light catching the edges that face it. Steepness measures how far the surface tilts from flat, 0 flat to 1 upright — the flat tops of a relief, or the steep sides where dirt cannot settle. Threshold is where the mask turns on, Softness how gradually, and Invert turns it over. Feed it a normal map: a height through Height to Normal, or a scanned one.

nodes.label: Perspective Pin
nodes.description: Pins the input into any four-cornered shape, in perspective, so straight lines stay straight: a label on a panel seen at an angle, a decal fitted to a face that is not square to the image, a plank laid into a parquet pattern. Drag the corners in the 2D View, or set them here, from the top left clockwise, in image widths. Outside leaves nothing beyond the quad — its edge antialiased however far it leans — or repeats the input there, as Sampling says.

nodes.label: Anti-Tile
nodes.description: Repeats a tileable input Repeat times across and down without the repeat showing — the fix for a ground, a wall or a fabric whose pattern reads as a grid once it covers a large surface. Every point of a triangle lattice shows its own randomly shifted copy, turned by up to Random Rotation of a full turn (leave it at 0 for anything with a grain or a direction), and copies blend into their neighbours. Blend Sharpness narrows each blend towards the nearest copy; Keep Contrast stops the blend from greying the detail out, so the result is as crisp as the input. Seed deals another arrangement. The result still tiles, and the input must: it is read wrapped.

nodes.label: FXAA
nodes.description: Smooths stepped edges by blurring along each edge rather than across it, so lines lose their stair steps while flat areas and fine texture stay as they are. Threshold is how much of a step counts as an edge; Span is how far the smoothing may reach, in pixels — stair steps are a pixel-sized fault, so it is meant for an image at the resolution it will be used at.

nodes.label: Denoise
nodes.description: Removes noise by averaging each pixel with the ones whose surroundings look like its own, rather than with whatever happens to be next to it. Detail that repeats survives where a blur would take it. Strength is how different two surroundings may be and still count; Radius is how far to look, in pixels — it works on noise at the scale of the pixels themselves, as a scan or a render has it, so it is meant for an image at the resolution it will be used at. Amount mixes back towards the input. Sampling says what lies past the edge.

nodes.label: Levels
nodes.description: Remaps a range of values to another, with a gamma bend between. Input Low and Input High are the values taken as black and white; Gamma above 1 brightens the mid tones and below 1 darkens them, the ends staying put; Output Low and Output High are what black and white become, so swapping them inverts. With Clamp on, values past the input range stop at the output range, as a picture’s levels do; off, they carry on along the same line, so values of any size — heights, HDR light — remap without being cut off. Each channel is remapped alike; alpha passes through.

nodes.label: Curves
nodes.description: Reshapes tones through curves: input across, output up. The RGB curve bends all channels alike; the R, G and B curves bend each on its own, before the RGB one. Click the square to add a point and drag it — up brightens the tones there, down darkens them; an S shape adds contrast. The curve runs smoothly through every point without overshooting any. Values past black or white carry on along the curve’s end slope, so HDR and heights are bent, not cut off. Alpha passes through.

nodes.label: Replace Color
nodes.description: Replaces colors within Tolerance of From with To. Softness widens the edge of the selection; Match selects by the whole color, or by Hue & Saturation alone so the lit and shaded sides of one paint are caught alike. Keep Shading moves the color rather than flattening it, so highlights and shadows survive. Color Key makes the same selection as a mask.

nodes.label: Color Key
nodes.description: White where the input is within Tolerance of Color, black elsewhere, fading across Softness between. Match by the whole color, or by Hue & Saturation alone, so the lit and shaded sides of one paint are picked alike. The same selection Replace Color makes, as a mask to drive anything else: a blend, a roughness change, a wear pass.

nodes.label: Gradient Map
nodes.description: Colorizes a grayscale input through a gradient: black takes the color at the left end, white the right. Add as many stops as you need, each with its own opacity, blended linearly, smoothly, as constant bands or along a spline.

nodes.label: HSL
nodes.description: Turns the hue by degrees and scales saturation and brightness. Model picks what brightness means: HSL’s Lightness runs from black through the pure color to white, so raising it pales a color towards white; HSV’s Value is the brightest channel, so raising it brightens a color without paling it. Saturation is taken in the same model. A color brighter than 1 keeps its brightness: it is adjusted as the same color at 1 and scaled back. Alpha passes through.

nodes.label: Dither
nodes.description: Ordered dithering: every pixel gets a threshold from a Bayer matrix, so a few levels can stand for many by mixing them. Levels cuts each channel to Levels steps from 0 to 1, a pixel taking the step above where its threshold says so — a flat 50 % grey at two levels is every other pixel white — for a pixel-art or print look without the bands Color Bands leaves. Subtract Threshold gives In minus the threshold, alpha included, ready for an Alpha Clip or a Step to turn into a stippled fade. Pattern is the matrix; Cell Size makes each of its cells that many pixels across. The pattern repeats every 2, 4 or 8 cells, so at the usual power-of-two sizes it tiles.

nodes.label: Temperature
nodes.description: Tints the image by the color of a light burning at Kelvin: warm below 6500 K, cool above, neutral at it. Brightness is held, so this shifts color without changing exposure. To take a cast out rather than put one in, use White Balance.

nodes.label: White Balance
nodes.description: Moves what counts as white, the way a camera does. Temperature runs cool to warm and Tint green to magenta, correcting a cast rather than adding one. The adaptation is done in LMS, so neutrals move and saturated colors are left much as they were.

nodes.label: Contrast
nodes.description: Scales values around Pivot with Amount as a linear slope: above 1 increases contrast, between 0 and 1 reduces it. The same contrast Color Correct applies, as a node of its own. Values outside 0 to 1 are scaled with the rest, not cut off.

nodes.label: Luminance
nodes.description: Luminance of the color, weighted by the luma coefficients (Rec.709 by default).

nodes.label: Colorspace Conversion
nodes.description: Converts a color from one space to another: RGB (sRGB-encoded, as a picture is stored), Linear (the light it stands for) or HSV (hue, saturation and value, each 0 to 1). HSV is reached from and left through RGB. The same space on both sides changes nothing; alpha is unchanged.

nodes.label: Color Correct
nodes.description: Hue, saturation, gamma, lift, gain, contrast and exposure in one node, applied in that order. Hue turns by degrees, as HSL’s does. Gain and Exposure scale the light itself, not the stored value: one stop of Exposure doubles the light, as a camera’s does, so a mid grey brightens without washing out. Values outside 0 to 1 pass through.

nodes.label: Color Bands
nodes.description: Flattens an image into bands: each channel quantised to Levels evenly spaced steps, the lowest at 0 and the highest at 1, so two levels give black and white and more give flat bands. Values are taken between 0 and 1 first. To snap numbers of any size to a grid instead, use Posterize under Math › Rounding.

nodes.label: Vibrance
nodes.description: Saturates the muted colors more than the vivid ones: a dull color gains as much as Amount asks, one already near full saturation hardly moves, so color comes up without anything clipping garish. Negative takes color out the same way, the dullest first.

nodes.label: Shadows/Highlights
nodes.description: Brightens or darkens the dark and the light ends of an image apart. Shadows lifts the darks when positive and deepens them when negative; Highlights brightens the lights when positive and pulls them back when negative, recovering detail a bright scan washed out. Each fades out towards the middle, which Midpoint sets, so the mid tones stay. Colors keep their hue: the brightness is changed, not each channel.

nodes.label: Extract
nodes.description: One channel of the input, by index. An index past the channels the input carries is an error.

nodes.label: Convert
nodes.description: Converts to another type: a single value fills every channel; fewer channels are padded with 0 (alpha 1); more are truncated. Int truncates a float or a vector toward zero, and makes a float an integer; Boolean is true for any non-zero value.

nodes.label: Combine 2
nodes.description: Joins two streams into one: two floats, a color or vector 3 plus a float, or two vector 2s.

nodes.label: Combine 3
nodes.description: Three floats as the channels of a color or vector 3.

nodes.label: Combine 4
nodes.description: Four floats as the channels of a color or vector 4.

nodes.label: Separate 2
nodes.description: The X and Y channels of a vector 2 as floats.

nodes.label: Separate 3
